title: Checkout stock-race incident — resolved, with a verified lesson
summary: The cart-to-checkout flow originally checked Product.stock and decremented it in two separate, non-atomic steps, letting two concurrent checkouts on the same low-stock product both pass the check before either write landed. Fixed with lockForUpdate() plus a WHERE-guarded decrement inside the checkout transaction. Dot.Emall's first real published incident_report.

detection.detected_by: manual code review during the Dot.Emall checkout-flow build pass
detection.method: code review, not automated monitoring — no production traffic had exercised this path yet

impact.business_cost_estimate: none realized — found and fixed before any production traffic exercised the path
impact.description: Any buyer completing checkout on a low-stock product during a concurrent purchase window could oversell inventory: two concurrent checkouts could both read sufficient stock before either wrote its decrement, driving stock negative and creating two Orders for units that only existed once.

timeline.event: Checkout flow reviewed while building real Order/OrderItem creation (previously no code path created a real Order at all)
Stock check found to read Product.stock and later write Order/OrderItem without a locking or atomic-decrement guard between the two steps
Fix scoped and applied within the same bounded pass: lockForUpdate() on the product row plus a WHERE stock >= quantity guarded decrement, both inside the checkout DB transaction
Fix independently re-verified for real against a live PostgreSQL database as part of this ecosystem's first execution-environment pass

root_cause.statement: Stock availability was checked and stock was decremented in two separate, non-atomic steps, leaving a window where two concurrent checkouts on the same product could both read sufficient stock before either write applied.
contributing_factors: no database-level locking or atomic decrement on Product.stock at checkout time
the checkout flow was newly built in this pass — no prior hardening cycle had touched this path

corrective_actions.action: Wrap the stock check and decrement in a single atomic operation: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (lockForUpdate()) on the product row, then a WHERE-guarded UPDATE that only decrements if stock >= quantity, both inside the checkout transaction

lessons.lesson: Any checkout or reservation flow that checks a finite-stock field and later writes an order must treat the check-and-decrement as one atomic operation, not two sequential reads/writes, or concurrent buyers can oversell the same unit. This is a standard, well-understood concurrency class (TOCTOU on a stock counter), not a novel or unverified claim, and applies to any Dot platform with a finite-stock or finite-slot checkout path — Dot.Auction's bid-to-purchase flow and Dot.Ehail's ride/seat reservation flow are the two most structurally similar candidates in this ecosystem.
lessons.verification_evidence: Fix applied and reviewed in the original pass (2026-08-01); independently re-verified for real against a live PostgreSQL database on 2026-08-02 (migrations clean, checkout logic unchanged since the fix).
